title: What LoRA trains
summary: Low-rank factors, the alpha scale, and merging at inference.

choices.text: You train a rank-8 copy of W from scratch, and alpha/r = 2 averages it with the frozen W, so the served layer is half old and half new.
You train two low-rank factors, but their product must stay a separate branch at inference, so every LoRA layer adds latency to the served model.
You train two low-rank factors whose product is added to W. Alpha is the rank of the second factor, so B is 16 columns wide while A has 8 rows.
You train two low-rank factors whose product, scaled by alpha/r, is added to W. At inference the product can be merged into W at no extra latency.
